output.brief: I did not collect any extra evidence; the initial evidence was enough. Analyzer B most likely produced one chance QC outlier. It was a single Level 2 potassium flag, and the repeat from the same vial passed straight away. Levels 1 and 3 were fine. QC means are unchanged since the lot change. Patient medians are normal, and 43 samples re-run on Analyzer A agreed within 0.10 mmol/L. QC was run on time, so the short-staffing theory is not supported. Ward 6's high potassiums are better explained by the tube outage (long transit times) and the extra renal patients. Half of those results came from Analyzer A. I'd recommend four things. Do not recall results, quarantine the lot or widen the limits. Return Analyzer B to potassium service, and consider an extra Level 2 QC per shift for a week as a precaution. Ask Ward 6 for repeat samples, and fix or work around the tube outage. I can't confirm a sampling glitch as the cause, so record it as unconfirmed. Confidence is moderate to high. The main residual risk is a subtle fault that this evidence would not show.
